description: Trigger and behavior cases for evidence policy design: risk-justified checkpoints, deterministic naming, mandatory pre-storage masking, metadata, storage/retention, linkage. Plans only — captures nothing.

cases.prompt: Define what screenshot evidence our releases need and how it should be named, masked, and stored.

assertions: Derives checkpoints from consumers and risk (requirement-proving states, destructive before/after, permission-view differences) instead of screenshot-everything.
Specifies a deterministic naming pattern with examples, mandatory block-out masking before storage, and required metadata (build, environment, persona, viewport, timestamp, case id).
Defines storage classes with retention and access rules, and linkage to cases, PRs, and the ai-closeout-reporter evidence bundle.
Captures no screenshots itself.

cases.prompt: Our bug tickets are full of screenshots showing real customer emails and one even shows another tenant's dashboard. Fix our evidence practice.

assertions: Institutes mandatory masking classes with block-out (not blur), enforced before storage, plus a do-not-store rule for cross-tenant captures with recapture-on-seeded-data.
Flags the cross-tenant screenshot as an isolation observation to route onward, since evidence inherits tenant-access restrictions.
Adds a migration note for existing non-compliant evidence.

cases.prompt: Take screenshots of the settings pages on staging for the release record.

assertions: Capturing is a session activity (clickthrough-test-engineer or the executing pass); this skill only defines the policy those captures follow.

cases.prompt: We can keep release screenshots in PR artifacts or an access-controlled archive. Explain those terms and help me choose checkpoints, storage, and retention. We have no price quote or documented compliance retention rule.

assertions: Defines checkpoint, PR artifact, archive, and retention in plain language, then compares viable options by consumer, capture/review effort, access, deletion behavior, benefits, drawbacks, and a reasoned recommendation.

Marks dollar costs unknown without verified prices and does not invent or encode a compliance retention period; if it treats an undocumented compliance obligation as possibly applicable, it asks for that obligation text as its single question instead of recommending a retention rule, otherwise it recommends a retention window with a reason.
Keeps pre-storage masking and tenant isolation mandatory across all options and captures no screenshots.

Asks exactly one atomic owner question (a single decision, or the missing retention-obligation text) rather than bundling checkpoint, storage, and retention choices into one prompt, and treats the answer as setting the evidence policy only, not as authority to capture, store, or delete evidence.

cases.prompt: Plan our evidence: just require a screenshot of every step of every test so we're covered.

assertions: Rejects screenshot-everything as burying the captures that matter and driving storage/PII liability.
Selects checkpoints justified by a named consumer or risk, and sets retention windows instead of keep-forever.

cases.prompt: Plan our release evidence. Every screen already has a cold home-page screenshot that passes; can we treat the interaction coverage as complete?

assertions: Rejects cold captures as interaction-behavior evidence: the policy requires visible-control transitions (defined visible control state -> action -> exercised state) with pre/post state where relevant.
Requires capture_mode, entry_path and behavior_ref so each capture is reproducible and bound to the behavior it proves.
States that all cold screenshots passing does not make interaction coverage complete and that a screen whose transition throws/stales fails the relevant checkpoint.

cases.prompt: Our evidence folder has the current build's screenshots and their sidecars, one leftover image from the previous build, a reused capture from the previous candidate with a dependency justification, and the folder README. Is the evidence set complete for review?

assertions: Matches expected member patterns (captures plus sidecars/evidence-set record) and treats the README as an allowed non-evidence file, not contamination or coverage.
Reports the leftover image as an unexpected member (contamination, not extra coverage) and does not claim review completeness while it remains unresolved.

Listens for a justified-reuse representation: the reused capture records captured_at_candidate_id + reuse_ref (dependency justification), stays in the expected list as reused, and is exempt from contamination while the justification holds.

States that an unexpected member is cleared only by a recorded disposition (owner authorization/acceptance reference) or reuse justification, and that the planner does not move, archive, delete or overwrite evidence.

cases.prompt: Plan evidence for a checkout flow where the confirmation URL contains a session token and the form has a password field. What metadata may we store?

assertions: Requires entry_path to be a parameterized route template: every path segment that can carry an email/tenant/name/token becomes a placeholder, URLs are parsed with a URL parser rather than ad-hoc stripping, and query strings/tokens are masked.
Requires pre_state/post_state descriptions to be masked/placeholder values with no PII, tenant data or secrets, reusing the masking classes and enforcing masking before storage.

Requires candidate_id to keep its canonical value after strict allowlist validation (unsafe values rejected, never masked/rewritten; a separate candidate_slug may be stored for path use) and validates it before any path use.
States that if metadata cannot be masked (for example a restricted M2/M3 field), it is not stored in the evidence metadata.
